tiers.silicon-qualified: An approved, evidence-backed silicon claim exists for this exact part and surface (a physical board was exercised and reviewed).
tiers.build-supported: The engine can emit a release-strict image for this surface on this device with no board required -- the AGRV2K fabric is identical across the family, so a fabric-logic-only capability qualified on one part carries to every part. This is a build claim, never a silicon claim.
tiers.recovered-only: Chipdb/decode data exists (or is expected to exist) for this surface, but no release-strict build path is admitted yet, or the surface has not been decoded/exercised on this part.
tiers.n/a: This surface does not apply to this part (e.g. PSRAM on a non-VH part).

notes: PREMISE (do not re-litigate): one AGRV2K fabric + RV32IMAFC core + boot ROM is shared
family-wide; only package/flash/PSRAM/analog surround differs per part. Building for a
part is never a silicon claim for that part -- a silicon claim is per-board and never
auto-transfers by package or pin number, even between two parts sharing one package.
AG32VF303CCT6 (AGRV2KL48) is the only silicon-qualified row: it is the reference dev
board with years of qualification ledgers (docs/KNOWN_GOOD_HARDWARE.md,
agamemnon/sdk/qualified_fabric_profiles.json). Every other part's config_accept is
'build-supported' rather than 'recovered-only' because claim_policy (T25,
agamemnon/engine/claim_policy.py) now admits a pad-free, fabric-logic-only build for
any package under release-strict -- physical/electrical surfaces (pad_out/pad_in/oe)
remain qualified on AGRV2KL48 only and stay 'recovered-only' elsewhere.
AG32VF407RGT6 (LQFP64) has an in-progress physical bring-up
(qualification/l64_bringup_evidence.jsonl, tasks T21-T24): pad-free config-accept and
an AHB transaction have been observed on real silicon, but the investigation is open
(an AHB read-value mismatch is unresolved) and deliberately not yet claimed as
qualified by that work itself -- this matrix keeps it 'build-supported' with a note
rather than promoting an in-flight, self-described non-conclusion.
That same evidence does NOT transfer to AG32VH303RCT6, the other LQFP64 part: package
evidence never transfers by pin number, and it does not transfer between two different
parts sharing one package either -- they are different physical dies.
AG32VF407VGT6 (LQFP100) is Brian's second physical board (AG32-Docs memory), but no
AGaMEMnon qualification evidence has been recorded for it yet; it is treated exactly
like an unqualified part until evidence lands.
